findingDetails.title: The promoted serving closure is not reproducible from its authored source: one served file has drifted and the parity gate exits 1
findingDetails.scopeProof: both paths are inside the branch diff's compiled-routing surface; the drift is a one-line diff between the two files, and git status --porcelain on both paths is empty, so the drift is committed rather than a dirty working tree
findingDetails.case: an operator runs compiled-route-sync.cjs --check before promoting the closure, gets exit 1, and cannot tell from the message whether the browser-use hub they are shipping caused it - the failing file belongs to the sk-doc hub, which this branch never touched, so the gate's red light is attributed to the wrong change and the real fix is not obvious

results.notes: Carried from iteration 3 and re-confirmed: the serving closure lists mcp-browser-use among 8 hubs with fileCount 69 matching len(files) 69, and generatedFrom resolves to an existing directory.
Carried from iteration 3. This iteration added no criterion evidence and contradicted none. The new P2 is in the promoted mirror of a sibling hub, not in any child phase tasks.md evidence.

noveltyJustification: One new P2 (weight 1) plus one refinement of the carried P1 R4-P1-001 at half weight (5 x 0.5 = 2.5), over a weighted total of 6: (1 + 2.5) / 6 = 0.583. The refinement is the admission gate passing where the recorded run says it failed, which sharpens R4-P1-001 into a stale-evidence defect rather than a broken gate. No new P0, so no ratio floor applies.
